question.problem: What is $\dfrac {x^2 + x - 6} {x-2}$ reduced to lowest terms?
question.worked_solution:
The numerator can be factored as $x^2+x-6= (x+3)(x-2).$ Cancelling out any common factors that appear in the numerator and the denominator, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+x-6}{x-2} & = \\ \frac{(x+3)(x-2)}{x-2} & = \\ \frac{(x+3)\cancel{(x-2)}}{\cancel{(x-2)}} & = \\ \frac{x+3}{1} & = \\ x+3 & .\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
